Entries record physically tested application SHAs, observed behavior, evidence boundaries, failed loops, commit/source audits, and the next allowed investigation scope. `USER_MARK` log entries are annotations and are never runtime proof by themselves.

### Attempt 6 and the newly established observation defect

- Observed order: req204 → showOp19/attach7 → first live draw at 420146403 → req217 classifies HIDDEN_UNKNOWN/WALK_TRUNCATED → hideOp20 local hide at 420146858 and removal at 420146877 → req221 → showOp21/attach8, add returns 420147010 → terminal hideOp22 removes it at 420147886.
- This proves an actual hide/re-add operation sequence, not the precise visual flicker seen by the user. Retries scheduled/fired are both zero for this attempt. A generic retry-loop explanation is unsupported.
- The second episode reports NO_DRAW_OBSERVED for root/shader/live. **It is unsafe to interpret this as "the second attachment never drew".**
- **PROVEN FROM SOURCE:** FluviKeyguardCardService.recordFirstRootDraw (f8 line 2082) and recordFirstShaderDraw (line 2100) validate attachment ownership, but emit all per-attachment FIRST_* diagnostic events only inside wakeTiming.firstRootDrawAt/firstShaderDrawAt == null. A nonterminal hide preserves the same WakeTiming. Consequently, a later accepted attachment in that wake can invoke genuine draw callbacks which the service does not publish. The cycle's first draw was already set by attach7.
- KeyguardCardWindow creates new attachment-owned observations; KeyguardHeaderMaterialView resets firstShaderDrawForAttach on onAttachedToWindow. The service is the downstream publication gate that conflates cycle-first aggregation with per-attachment first observations. The relevant gate was already present in the parent; do not call this a newly introduced f8 regression.
- **Required repair boundary:** preserve cycle-first/earliest summary values, while independently recording each current attachment's first root/current-material/live observation once. Preserve session/wake/attach/show-operation identity and rejection of delayed old callbacks. Do not reset the cycle's first timestamps on reattach.
- **Existing false-green gap:** cycleFirstLiveSurvivesLaterAttachmentRemovedWithoutDrawing injects synthetic diagnostic events directly; it does not exercise the service callback gate. KeyguardFirstDrawOwnerTest checks identity only. Production-window instrumentation exercises real retained roots, material controller, bootstrap commit, live shader and reattach, but callbacks terminate in test lambdas, bypassing service publication. It uses an activity-backed application-panel window, not Nothing's keyguard policy.
- A new baseline-red test must drive two genuinely drawn attachments through the production service publication path (or a narrow extracted owner actually used by it), keeping one wake. Add true-no-draw second-attach, duplicate and stale callback controls. A synthetic reducer-only test cannot close this gap.
- WALK_TRUNCATED has multiple source reasons: 96-node per-window cap, null advertised child, or a caught acquisition exception. Attempt6 visits 43 nodes total; the cap is not established as the cause. Retain bounded reason/provenance without logging private accessibility text.
- Full request221 acquisition/application evidence and episode-owned actual draw cadence are missing from the exported handoff. The first showing inspection is not a substitute for the second show's cause.

## 2026-11-12 — detached ORB prewarm handoff drain after API35 RED

Application correction: `22e5a617` (`fix(keyguard): drain detached ORB prewarm handoff`), parent `ef366946`.

Why: `ef366946` correctly used the actual bounded isolated-renderer owner, but retained its detached `READY_FOR_MAIN` result. A detached frame has no publication target, so it could occupy a fixed-pool handoff slot indefinitely.

Evidence: exact-source workflow [43215481141](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/actions/runs/43215481141) compiled and ran the API35 native suite, then failed before the Human APK job. Its retained [runtime artifact](https://github.com/elizerpist/exptv2/actions/runs/43215481141/artifacts/13944806276) records `rapid-cycle-24` attach `30/84`: produced/published stayed `401/397`, all three slots stayed compositor-owned, and drops rose `1141 -> 2194` over the deadline. This is a pool-progress failure, not evidence of a static shader phase. The prior `04e229c` artifact completed the corresponding cycle after compositor ownership reduced and producer output advanced.

Changed: a detached success still proves that the actual `HardwareBufferRenderer` allocation and slot-local shader initialized, and still emits `MATERIAL_ISOLATED_BACKEND_PREPARED`, but now immediately returns its unauthorised result via the existing fence-safe `dropReady` path. Fixed buffers, renderer instances and slot-local shaders remain resident. No detached frame is published, made visible, or relabeled as the next attachment. The direct instrumentation test now requires zero detached ready, in-flight and compositor-owned slots before first show.

Independent observations: Canvas and isolated compositor crops timed out with a white/off-target crop while the isolated producer sample was valid. That remains a compositor-observation fixture boundary pending the focused rerun; it is not a RuntimeShader-freeze diagnosis. The service fixture timed out only after the slot-progress condition above.

Validation so far: `git diff --check` PASS; clean-source `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` PASS; clean-source `scripts/test-fluvi-fast.sh` PASS; local Android Kotlin compilation NOT RUN to completion because Termux ARM/proot cannot start the host AAPT2 daemon. Compatible API35 validation is required.

Rejected hypotheses: no change to shader math, effect selection, per-frame shader construction, visibility/privacy policy, or the Main inspection schedule. The Nothing A142 89 ms Main handoff remains unattributed.

Physical validation: PENDING — USER ONLY.

## 2026-11-12 — actual isolated ORB preparation candidate (`ef366946`)

**Why.** The frozen `04e229c` phone exports establish a real preparation
mismatch: `prepareRetainedView` prepared source/program artifacts and a
disposable `HardwareRenderer`/`ImageReader`, but did not configure the
isolated `KeyguardOrbBufferRenderer` which owns the eventual three-buffer
pool and slot-local shaders. The FULL export separately establishes an
83 ms inspection plus 89 ms Main-handoff interval for withdrawal request 261;
it does not establish what occupied Main during that interval.

**Evidence reviewed.** Application baseline `04e229c64e560bef9d49972c3413d1115fc36c41`;
reviewer-only journal head `0bc1a54081fe816d75a55c634f960760d10eec96`.
The original frozen LIGHT/FULL exports embedded above remain the source
evidence: LIGHT 30,534 bytes SHA-256
`917088d296edfe82bdc3d888ec9cce2d5e3142891e1e78088dfba49c575b09d1`;
FULL 29,079 bytes SHA-256
`903d0a42809e95c3795260afe491accb2eea0736d3683e0e997e6b10f277ae66`.
They are truncated and do not observe physical presentation/removal. The
matching Dart-only graph was queried at tooling `6b3298f3303b3f27c7a523763110971660c8afb9`
(source `04e229c`): `KeyguardTimingCaptureBridge` reports 8 references
(3 production/5 test), and `KeyguardTimingCaptureSnapshot` 12 production
references. This is navigation evidence only; native Kotlin ownership was
audited directly through service → window → material controller → isolated
renderer → diagnostics/tests.

**Changed.** `KeyguardCardMaterialController.prepare` now selects supported
animated ORB-only input while detached and reconciles the *same* bounded
isolated renderer used after attachment. Its worker performs one real
detached frame, retaining the existing single READY frame but no parent layer
or visibility authority. A fresh authorized attachment still receives a new
lease and must publish a current frame before it can replace the View
bootstrap. `MATERIAL_ISOLATED_BACKEND_PREPARED` records that actual detached
completion with program, lease and dimensions; this is not a presentation
marker. The old disposable GPU warmup remains only for routes that still need
the legacy View path; it is no longer misrepresented as isolated-backend
readiness.

The same commit adds FULL-only, bounded correlation for a Main handoff of at
least one display interval: immutable `System.nanoTime` request/entry
endpoints and at most three overlapping *Fluvi-owned* Main scopes, with
omission/eviction/coverage flags. Empty or incomplete evidence is explicitly
not an attribution to RenderThread, GPU, Binder, framework, or scheduler.
LIGHT preserves scalar timing without copying spans.

**Regression intent.**

- `retainedPreparationWarmsActualIsolatedBackendBeforeFirstShow` is a
  baseline RED against `04e229c`: old service preparation cannot produce a
  detached isolated output because `isolatedOrbRequested` is still false.
  It requires before-show actual output, zero publication, and a distinct
  current output after authorized attachment.
- `fullCapturePinsBoundedSlowMainHandoffEvidenceInTheCausalSpine` verifies
  that bounded attribution fields survive raw-event pressure through the
  causal spine.

**Validation at commit.**

- PASS: `git diff --check`.
- PASS: `bash scripts/verify-fluvi-boundaries.sh`.
- NOT RUN locally: `proot-distro login ubuntu -- bash -lc '... ./gradlew
  --no-daemon :app:compileDebugKotlin :app:compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin
  --stacktrace'` reached `:app:processDebugResources` but failed before
  Kotlin compilation because the cached x86_64 AAPT2 binary cannot start in
  ARM64/proot (`Exec failed, error: 2`). This is the established host
  limitation, not a PASS and not source-compile evidence.
- PENDING: x86_64 Android compilation, lower API35 instrumentation, real
  service fixture, core/Flutter gates, Human APK job, and physical test.

**Rejected/non-claims.** This does not claim that the 04e phone lag is fixed,
that the 89 ms handoff is GPU work, that local hide submission is physical
removal, or that a green test would establish phone pacing. No dashboard,
launcher widget, shader equations, privacy policy, input handling, pool bound,
or stale lease authority was changed.

**Physical validation: PENDING — USER ONLY.**

### Proven failing boundary and repair

Chain: callbacks → queue/freshness/gate → reader/classifier → show decision → retained window → material controller/view/clock → attachment-owned draw callback → **service publication gate** → worker reducer/export.

`recordFirstRootDraw` / `recordFirstShaderDraw` previously emitted FIRST events only when `WakeTiming`'s cycle-first field was null. Nonterminal withdrawal retained WakeTiming, so a second attachment could really draw while its downstream FIRST events were suppressed. Window observations and material first-shader flags were already attachment-owned. Old diagnostics tests injected FIRST events directly; real-window tests ended at test lambdas, bypassing the defective service boundary.

Unit 1 extracted the existing condition into production `KeyguardDrawPublication`, used by the service, before changing behavior. Baseline RED: second genuinely owned attachment failed publication (**3 tests, 1 failure**). Corrected owner binds serviceSession/wake/attach, publishes ROOT and SHADER once per current attachment, rejects stale/duplicate/revoked callbacks, and retains independent earliest cycle fields. A second attachment removed before drawing produces no synthetic timestamps. Real-window CARD and ORB tests now route actual draw callbacks through this same production owner and original `KeyguardFirstDrawOwner.accepts` gate. They exercise real WindowManager/ViewRoot traversal and real frame commitment, not manual `onBootstrapFrameCommitted()` acknowledgement.

### Implemented measurement contract and impact inventory

- `KeyguardDrawGapEvidence`: fixed three primitive slots per material View; exact previous successful shader-traversal end and current start/end, latest clock frame/entry/owned-work exit, prior callback entry, callbacks since last draw, CPU/configure/Canvas-call durations, current program and pixel extent. First/unpaired/coalesced observations, sampling breaks, rejected ownership and non-retained gap counts stay explicit. No output cannot become smoothness evidence. Initial draw has no invented callback. Non-live/bootstrap/static/fallback/pause time breaks pairing; hidden idle and another attachment/capture cannot form a live gap.
- `KeyguardMaterialClock` uses its existing callback/schedule sequence; primitive SAM avoids three new boxed timestamp arguments per callback. Controller still owns exactly one clock. View samples only successful actual hardware shader geometry; transition may submit previous+current programs, so exported `currentProgram` is not a claim that only one shader ran. No per-frame formatting, queueing, lock, persistence, file read, platform-state read or independent heartbeat.
- `KeyguardMainWorkEvidence`: service-owned Main-thread ring32, max3 overlapping own spans selected without sorting/all-slot object allocation. Kinds1=system fast-gate reads,2=inspection apply,3=diagnostic ingress. Records request/session/Linux thread ID, elapsed endpoints and whole-scope CPU. Nested/overlapping spans must NOT be summed. Ring completeness only concerns these scopes, not arbitrary MainLooper work. Unsupported CPU is explicit (-1 internally, NA/UNOBSERVED on export), never fabricated zero.
- `KeyguardCardWindow` passes attachment generation/provider to its retained controller. Actual View/controller detach both revoke measurement ownership; capture-token changes cannot reactivate a detached owner. Existing root/lifecycle/first-draw/frame-commit/bootstrap publication is unchanged. No new listener registration, View retention or renderer clock.
- Service snapshots only after local hide/removal; formatting remains in deferred diagnostic-worker fields. `KeyguardCardSettings` extends only the existing summary/export path: optional whole `DRAW_GAP` rows, balanced episode/sample selection AFTER critical show/hide causes, bounded3 records/surface and1,200characters/record. Generic160character truncation must not cut numeric records. Producer omission, bounded-source rejection and export omission remain distinct. Complete UTF-8 report cap stays32,768bytes, counting header/legend/metadata/footer; optional gap omission cannot pretend an actual draw did not occur.
- Native consumers explicitly searched: service→window→controller→orb/background View→clock/cadence; service→existing deferred diagnostics→episode export. Controller has one production Window caller; material Views are the retained XML orb/background plus tests; clock has controller as its only production caller. New helpers are native-only and have direct production consumers and focused tests. Flutter bridge/console transport remains untouched; launcher and financial producer consumers were checked and not modified. This inventory is NOT Kotlin SCIP coverage.
- Layout/layer audit: no XML/resource dimension, WindowManager flag/type/z-order, clipping/paint geometry, accessibility description, input/touch/drag, saved-position, privacy/full/neutral or financial-content change. One retained root and original controller/clock ownership. Observation IDs supplement, never grant, session/wake/visibility/interaction/attach/show authority.

Clock meanings: all new Ns endpoints use `System.nanoTime`/the existing Choreographer timebase; uptimeMs origins stay separate, with no cross-domain subtraction. `cbOut` is the end of owned callback work before probe bookkeeping, NOT all handler execution. Canvas-call duration is CPU-side submission, NOT GPU duration or physical display. `drawObserverNs` measures numeric bookkeeping scopes only; timer calls and total observer perturbation are additional. [Android callback contract](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/Choreographer.FrameCallback), [thread CPU contract](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/Debug#threadCpuTimeNanos()). Flutter build/raster FrameTiming is N/A to this native renderer.

### First unresolved boundary and experiment

The old `TestPanelWindowManager` explicitly rewrites TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY to TYPE_APPLICATION_PANEL with an Activity token. Its automatic commit/LIVE tests remain useful lower-level contracts but omit Android service binding, the service token, real keyguard callbacks/classification and transition work. Portal/mode also differed. That coverage gap is proven; it is NOT itself the phone stall cause.

New `KeyguardServiceOverlayInstrumentationTest` obtains UiAutomation with DONT_SUPPRESS_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES, enables the actual production component on the disposable emulator, publishes through existing settings/material APIs while unlocked, and waits for normal screen/keyguard inspection to authorize the real overlay. There is no injected MAIN decision, fake WindowManager, synthetic commit/promotion or replacement clock. Known inputs match dualTide/Portal generated program24f2d163…08df,ORB/orbOnly,168×168at420dpi. Unprovided palette/Portal controls are explicitly synthetic, not falsely called exact phone settings.

Scenarios: actual service-cold first attach; ten-second quiet LIVE interval with no fixture polling/screenshots/IPC inside it; crop-only nonempty/moving output checks where capture is available; actual tap ownership; unlock/removal; warm attach; rapid wake/unlock during possible acquisition; authorized re-entry. Tests assert liveness/actual output and ownership, not invented FPS/smoothness thresholds. Existing panel tests remain unchanged. Secure-keyguard/biometric/OEM coverage is unavailable here.

The CI-only Perfetto lane requests sched/thread-state, ViewRoot/WM/ATrace, RenderThread, logcat and SurfaceFlinger FrameTimeline for a finite120s/64MiB capture. Host timeout110s bounds a blocked fixture. No profiler or extra instrumentation is added to the human runtime. Test-scoped KGProbe markers and monotonic/boot anchors identify sampling work; capture/episode identities are saved. Trace clock snapshots must be used across suspend, not naive boot-minus-monotonic subtraction. Coverage/drop counts and actual trace must be inspected; file existence alone is not success. Official sources checked: [UiAutomation](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/UiAutomation#FLAG_DONT_SUPPRESS_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES), [Perfetto CLI](https://perfetto.dev/docs/reference/perfetto-cli), [FrameTimeline](https://perfetto.dev/docs/data-sources/frametimeline).

### Concrete next production repair — prescribed, not a new investigation assignment

Implement a narrowly scoped system-gate ownership refactor in the native service:

1. Separate system-state acquisition from the pure gate decision. Add an injectable production `KeyguardSystemStateReader` and one service-owned bounded `KeyguardSystemGateSampler` (names may follow local conventions). Recurring system reads run on a dedicated serial I/O lane, independent of the potentially blocked accessibility-tree lane; at most one active read plus one latest pending request. No per-frame polling, per-event job fan-out, main-thread wait/join, shared blocking lock, timed retry storm or privilege change.
2. Carry immutable request/result identity: serviceSession, wakeGeneration, visibilityEpoch, interactionEpoch, attachGeneration, monotonically ordered gateRequestId, capture/read times and reason. These values are identity, not a TTL permission cache. Do not hold AccessibilityNodeInfo/Event or View objects in this lane. Late Binder completion is rejected by identity; coroutine cancellation is not assumed to interrupt Binder.
3. Main retains exclusive authority over window, epochs, decision, retries and rendering. Direct SCREEN_OFF/USER_PRESENT, interrupt/disconnect/disable and privacy tightening invalidate pending positive publication and hide/redact immediately without waiting for a sampler/tree read. Privacy tightening must never attach a new root.
4. Replace recurring main remote calls in callback/retry/reconciliation/UNKNOWN/steady same-authority inspection paths with local identity checks plus bounded sampling. Preserve relevant event classification and immediate terminal branches. Already-visible same-permission inspection may maintain existing content, but cannot turn an old positive sample into permission for a new attach or new disclosure.
5. Keep the final fresh system-state guard at each real new attach or permission-increasing transition. Read one fresh snapshot at that commit boundary and feed both fast-exclusion/final-gate policy from it; remove duplicate same-boundary reads. This rare main boundary is deliberate to retain apply-time eligibility after a worker result waits in the main queue. Actual new financial-data publication keeps its existing current-state/privacy guard in this task.
6. A valid current negative surface result performs local withdrawal before retry-eligibility acquisition; detached UNKNOWN still preserves compatible pending work and does not churn epochs. Current system exclusion is a separate observation, not a stale surface payload's authority: a stale payload cannot suppress a fresh current exclusion, while an old-generation negative cannot detach a newer attachment. Never coalesce an already accepted terminal exclusion away behind a positive.
7. No diagnostic-only final candidate. Demonstrate the production parent failing and the repair passing a controlled delayed-reader regression: main/actual retained-orb progress while the recurring provider call remains blocked; immediate terminal hide/redaction during that pending call; stale positive rejection; old-wake negative rejection; event-burst bound; unchanged fresh final-show authorization. Pair pure-policy tests with real service/window output. Do not simulate successful shader output with counter-only mocks.
8. Preserve renderer/program/palette/phase, single clock/root, window flags/input/z-order, surface classifier/freshness, financial semantics, launcher pipeline and all dashboard milestones. No FPS cap, lower resolution, static bitmap, delayed hide, permissive UNKNOWN, permission cache TTL or weakened test assertion.

SCREEN_OFF, USER_PRESENT, interrupt and opt-out still call the immediate terminal path; root invisibility/input withdrawal precede removal/cleanup. ### Changed contracts and retained ownership

`AndroidKeyguardSystemStateReader` owns the actual public platform getters; immutable `KeyguardSystemState` distinguishes unavailable/transitional state from definite OFF. `KeyguardSystemStateSampler` has one active worker call and one latest pending request, independent of the one-wide tree reader. Every request carries session/wake/visibility/interaction/attach identities, gate ID and causal timestamps. No live View, Event or node is retained. Main never joins or holds a lock behind the reader. Disposal revokes publication and submission; it does not pretend to cancel a blocked platform call.

```text
Main event/retry -> bounded system I/O lane -> Main identity check
tree inspection -> Main local stale check -> same-permission update
                                      -> ONE fresh admission read for attach/increase
direct terminal/privacy signal -> Main invalidate + hide/redact (no worker wait)
Main retained root -> existing controller -> existing single material clock
```

`FluviKeyguardCardService` routes recurring callbacks/retries/stale-payload exclusion checks to the sampler. Existing inspection-worker signals can maintain an already-authorized same-permission attachment, but cannot grant a new attachment or increased disclosure. One fresh Main ADMISSION snapshot remains for those transitions and is reused across final policies. A separate fresh Main PUBLICATION guard remains for actual new financial data, after cheap local stale rejection. Both can still block Main by design; they are counted separately from recurring acquisition. This is not a promise to remove all Main platform work.

Terminal SCREEN_OFF/USER_PRESENT/interrupt/opt-out invalidates before local invisibility and removal. Sampler revocation also protects an idempotent repeated terminal call. Privacy tightening redacts an attached root without system acquisition and cannot attach a detached root. Current visible UNKNOWN withdraws before retry eligibility work; hidden UNKNOWN preserves pending inspection/freshness. Completed cause requests are excluded from future-work suppression via `KeyguardCardInspectionQueue.hasCurrentWork`. Renewed work reacquires under new authority rather than reusing an old answer.

Production files: service, new reader/state/sampler, queue, signals/policy, and registry test accessor. Test files: sampler/admission unit suite, queue regression and real-service fixture; a local JVM harness compiles these actual production components. `TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY`, flags, z-order, layout/paint/clipping bounds, tap/drag and saved positions remain unchanged. No parallel ViewRoot, animation clock, financial store or recurring polling loop was added.

Exact current source mechanism: `FluviKeyguardCardService.applyInspection` special-cases only HIDDEN_UNKNOWN. HIDDEN_OCCLUDED enters the general `hideImmediately(...)` branch with default `terminalWake=true`. That method clears the system sampler, ends `wakeCycleOwner`, increments wakeEpoch, cancels retry and calls `inspectionQueue.clearPending()`. `processInspectionQueue` completes active35 only AFTER apply returns; its queue.complete35 therefore has no successor. No automatic fresh reconciliation survives. This path is also present in1f source. It is an actual lost-reconciliation defect, not a hypothesis that the surface classifier should accept a foreign window.

NOT PROVEN: which package owned window5, whether req36 specifically represented its removal, or whether req36 would have returned MAIN. ### Confirmed cause, precise RED and correction

The failing owner was `FluviKeyguardCardService.applyInspection`: OCCLUDED used generic `hideImmediately` with its terminal default. That ended wake ownership and cleared pending inspection before `inspectionQueue.complete(active)` could advance. The reviewer req35/req36 sequence proves deletion of unserved intent, not misclassification or that req36 would necessarily return MAIN.

The baseline eb26d4d8 preserves21's lifecycle behavior and adds only an inert optional production-boundary seam plus actual-service regression. Run42920244421 failed at the exact intended assertion, “Recoverable occlusion erased the newer unserved inspection,” AFTER establishing current negative ownership and a pending newer event. The failure crossed actual classifier → Main apply → actual queue state, not a copied Boolean policy or setup timeout. Old tests did not cover a newer event arriving immediately before delivery of an older recoverable occlusion.

```text
old: current OCCLUDED → terminal hide → end wake / erase pending → no successor
new, hidden: current OCCLUDED → remain excluded → complete cause → pending starts
new, visible: revoke + local hide → copy pending intent to NEW authority/request
              → new acquisition → fresh MAIN + admission → one retained root
terminal: off/unlock/disable/interrupt/disconnect → invalidate + cancel recovery
```

Runtime commit7099f6c0 changes only service routing/intent ownership and the narrow awaiting diagnostic identity. `applyInspection` routes UNKNOWN/OCCLUDED through `handleRecoverableSurface`; `scheduleEvaluation` accepts an immutable reconciliation intent; `KeyguardCardInspectionRequest.reacquireAfterWithdrawal` assigns a new ID/enqueue/visibility/interaction/attach owner while preserving original event/callback/trigger/capture and outstanding freshness. It rejects another service/wake. Visible withdrawal never reuses the old acquired answer. Already-hidden exclusion does not hide again, end the wake or churn epochs. The active cause is never counted as future pending work. Finite16/32/64ms fallback and its budget are unchanged; repeated exclusion does not replenish them. Exhaustion waits for an event. Actual successful show retains the existing budget reset.

Terminal default/cancellation and fresh admission remain intact. No cached positive grants a new attachment or greater disclosure. Current privacy redaction and financial-publication guards remain. Credential/shade policy, foreign-window acceptance, cache/prefetch and incomplete-snapshot rejection were NOT altered. Diagnostics retain the OCCLUDED classification and do not inflate UNKNOWN counters.

Main remains sole presentation/window/visibility/interaction/retry owner. The existing recurring system sampler stays off Main, independently bounded to one active plus one latest pending; the tree reader keeps the same bound. No thread joins, parallel tree reader, new polling, renderer/clock, permission or process was introduced. One retained root/controller/clock remains. Session/wake/visibility/interaction/attach identities guard delayed results. First-draw publication is invalidated before real removal; old negatives cannot withdraw a newer root and old positives cannot reattach after terminal exclusion.

`TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY`, window flags/z-order, fixed CARD/ORB dimensions, clipping/antialiasing, touch/long-press/drag ownership, positions, material program/palette/phase/resolution and launcher widgets are unchanged. ### Source diagnosis and selected implementation contract

PROVEN structural coupling:
KeyguardCardMaterialController owns a Main Choreographer clock; its callback calls orb.frame/background.frame; frame invalidates the View; KeyguardHeaderMaterialView.onDraw records the shader into the same WindowManager ViewRoot rendering path. FluviKeyguardCardService application of negative/positive answers and KeyguardCardWindow visibility/window operations also require Main. A graphics wait in that ViewRoot therefore delays both frame production and service presentation control. Current trace executes this coupling; cheap draw CPU does not remove it.

UNPROVEN: that this one mechanism explains every Nothing stall, the303ms first traversal, the55ms callback-body outlier, all remote accessibility acquisition latency or delayed system event delivery. No claim that Android public APIs guarantee a particular phone frame rate. No phone performance improvement is asserted before implementation and physical validation.

The selected next task is a bounded implementation of render/control isolation for API34+ animated standalone ORB. It is an architectural repair of the demonstrated coupling and a falsifiable candidate for the phone symptom, not an open-ended diagnostics-only task or a promised complete cure. Its correctness and performance contracts must be RED/GREEN tested on the actual overlay before release.

Concrete design:
1. Keep the existing service, fresh admission, privacy, one WindowManager root, gestures and pending-work/epoch policies. CARD, <=API33, static/OFF, launcher widgets and dashboard keep their established routes.
2. For API34+ animated ORB, replace the active per-frame View invalidation path with one dedicated HandlerThread/Choreographer producer rendering the canonical AGSL through RenderNode + platform HardwareBufferRenderer into a fixed three-slot HardwareBuffer pool. No second concurrent animation clock/backend.
3. The worker owns mutable RuntimeShader/Paint/RenderNode and all render invocation/fence work. Main never waits for render completion, fences, worker joins or resource destruction. All HardwareBufferRenderer instances still share Android's RenderThread; this is control-path isolation, not a private GPU or guaranteed faster shader.
4. Publish GPU-ready buffers to a non-input child SurfaceControl parented to the EXISTING Fluvi overlay root using its AttachedSurfaceControl. Do not parent to SystemUI or replace the visibility authority/window type. BuildReparentTransaction has a nullable result; unavailable attachment stays hidden and event-recoverable.
5. Main alone creates/reparents/shows/hides child layers and authorizes an exact session/wake/visibility/attach/content/privacy lease. The worker may only update buffers on its leased layer; it never shows/reparents a layer. Each withdrawal/privacy invalidation retires that layer; never recycle its identity into a new authority epoch. A raced old setBuffer cannot make a hidden/unparented old layer visible.
6. Perform immediate child hide/reparent-null from Main before root removal/slow cleanup. Cancel current lease before async work. Do not queue hide behind rendering. Defer GPU object cleanup safely. Bound retired resources and replacements globally; do not allocate new pools/layers indefinitely during rapid wake/mode changes.
7. Use exact measured orb dimensions, RGBA8888 premultiplied transparency, existing circle/AA, canonical profile/phase/180ms semantic transition. Full-to-neutral changes revoke old presentation before new publication and never crossfade financial colours.
8. Do not send unsignaled producer fences into a compositor queue ahead of hide: readiness/fence checks are worker-side; release fences also govern safe reuse. Three slots with explicit FREE/RENDERING/READY/COMPOSITOR_OWNED/RETIRED states; one in-flight render and latest-only desired state, no catch-up queue. Clear transparent pixels every frame. Size and usage support checked without lowering visual fidelity.
9. Prepare this SAME bounded rendering backend offscreen while detached; preparation grants no visibility. A ready, current, authorized buffer need not wait for an unrelated bootstrap View commit. If not ready, preserve safe fallback and later automatic promotion; late results cannot revive retired authority. Preserve legacy bootstrap tests for the legacy backend.
10. Add backend-specific CPU-record/GPU-ready/buffer-submission evidence. Do not rename old CPU-draw counters as physical presentation, compare old/new incompatible timings, or turn UNOBSERVED into0.

Platform HardwareBufferRenderer is API34, exposes obtainRenderRequest().draw(executor, callback), shares RenderThread, preserves existing buffer contents unless cleared, and does not close the caller's HardwareBuffer. SurfaceControl setBuffer requires COMPOSER_OVERLAY and GPU_SAMPLED_IMAGE usage; render targets also require GPU_COLOR_OUTPUT. Its release callback/fence controls reuse. These documented contracts justify the API design; they do not establish a phone root cause.

## 2026-11-11 — R-NATIVE-RENDER-ISOLATION-01 implementation candidate

### Basis and bounded claim

- Application baseline: `dc591498316ac647ca2873c7a0f7e72d12fd85ff`; documentation handoff: `441aaa53322ab6113b1fd9789d08ca764a9edda4`. The branch was fetched and the documentation-only descendant was reconciled before editing. Untracked user failure-evidence directories remain untouched.
- The complete accessible rule assets were reread before this change: prompt writer SHA-256 `f5f3f324bfea16cf5740ae15d565c5ce8ed6d5526e0705d321a004ad0adf9297`; widget addendum SHA-256 `dc695dde88fab03765c03b1fd8b86d3b2683832d8c0eec73362d21a197b5992c`. The numbered uploads were unavailable; the accessible copies match the hashes recorded in the preceding journal entry. `MILESTONE_COMMITS.md`, historical failures and the R-NATIVE contract were reviewed.
- This is an application implementation, not a claim of Nothing-device improvement. The confirmed architectural defect is recurring ORB View invalidation/draw submission sharing the accessibility-service Main owner with hide/show control. The emulator trace demonstrates that coupling; it does **not** prove every `edd89809-1994-49af-b87d-5fe208c5ac2b` phone gap has the same cause. Remote accessibility reads, event delivery and physical compositor/panel endpoints remain separate and unobserved.

### Changed production ownership

- Added `KeyguardOrbBufferRenderer`: API-34+ only, one dedicated `HandlerThread`/`Choreographer`, thread-confined `RuntimeShader`/`Paint`/`RenderNode`, and one fixed three-slot `RGBA_8888` HardwareBuffer pool (`GPU_COLOR_OUTPUT | GPU_SAMPLED_IMAGE | COMPOSER_OVERLAY`). It uses platform `HardwareBufferRenderer.obtainRenderRequest().draw(executor, callback)` and clears transparent contents before every antialiased canonical ORB draw.
- Main remains the sole owner of the retained `TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY`, authority, touch/drag, layer creation, parenting, visibility, privacy revocation and retirement. The producer may render and report a ready buffer only; it cannot show, reparent or recreate a layer. A non-input `SurfaceControl` child is parented through the existing root's `AttachedSurfaceControl.buildReparentTransaction`; no extra WindowManager window or SystemUI parent is introduced.
- Each buffer publication carries an exact lease: attachment, generation, material/visual/program identity and dimensions. Main rejects stale completions before `setBuffer`; hide/privacy/detach hides and reparents-null before root removal. Old render/compositor slots are retained only until their worker callback/release fence, never reused by a new lease and never waited on by Main. The pool is bounded to one in-flight render and latest-only desired state.
- `KeyguardCardMaterialController` selects this route only for API-34+ animated standalone `ORB`/`orbOnly`. CARD, static/OFF, API-33-and-below and all legacy bootstrap paths remain on their current route. The isolated route stops the Main material clock and leaves the palette-correct retained View bootstrap visible until the first current buffer is submitted; it then hides that View ORB so exactly one producer is visible. A producer failure retires the layer and returns to the pre-existing View renderer, not a permanent static substitute.
- The isolated worker preserves current phase across detach/reattach and carries the existing bounded 180-ms non-privacy semantic transition using immutable old/current scenes and, where available, their bounded old/current artifacts. Privacy full-to-neutral retires the old layer before a neutral buffer can publish.
- Material/service diagnostic fields now distinguish isolated produced/published/dropped buffers and worker completion gaps from legacy View callbacks and CPU shader calls. They remain submission/worker evidence, not physical presentation timestamps.

### Regression coverage and current validation

- Added a real window lifecycle execution-isolation test: after isolated output exists, a test-only renderer-boundary barrier holds the next worker frame; Main performs normal withdrawal and immediate reattachment before release. The reattached root must obtain its own current output, so an old lease cannot publish into it. This is an execution-isolation contract, explicitly not an injected reproduction of a Nothing GPU driver stall.
- Added an isolated ORB PixelCopy liveness test requiring changing compositor pixels, actual isolated submissions, no legacy Main clock callbacks, one in-flight producer and at most three compositor-owned buffers.
- Updated the existing API-35 actual accessibility-overlay service fixture so the phone-matched standalone ORB route requires `HardwareBufferRenderer/SurfaceControl`, current-attachment isolated output, material identity, nonempty cropped material and changing pixels. It remains an emulator/activity fixture and is not target-device smoothness acceptance.

### Follow-up: producer-failure fallback before delivery

- Post-commit lifecycle review found that a failed isolated producer still left `isolatedOrbRequested` true and could retain the legacy controller in `BOOTSTRAP`, which risks a non-animating compatibility fallback. The source is corrected before final delivery: a failed visual key selects the already-prepared legacy View route in `LIVE`, clears the bootstrap token, and suppresses repeated attempts for that exact visual key. A materially different visual key may make one bounded fresh isolated attempt. This is a correctness/liveness correction, not a device-performance claim; CI is rerun from its follow-up application SHA.

### Follow-up: exact-source API-35 RED and isolated LIVE ownership repair

- Exact-source CI run `42949468752` exposed a genuine production-fixture RED on `2e9ed4bbc2e219e83d36aeff1586dfca0366ee84`: `connectedProductionServiceRendersPortalOrbAcrossRealKeyguardCycles` timed out waiting for current `LIVE` output. The Human APK job was correctly skipped.
- Retained job artifact `13825420828` shows the buffer producer was not idle: the current attachment published 132 buffers. Yet the service diagnostic remained `BOOTSTRAP`; this is an ownership/state defect, not evidence that the test should accept a bootstrap as live output.
- Cause: the API-34 isolated path deliberately bypasses the legacy View bootstrap commit, but its first matching `SurfaceControl.setBuffer` publication did not itself clear the legacy bootstrap state. A real completed, Main-authorized buffer transaction is the corresponding live boundary for this backend.
- Candidate correction: only after the existing exact attached/current-lease checks succeed, `onIsolatedOrbFirstPublished` now sets `LIVE`, clears the legacy bootstrap token/commit bit, then hides the bootstrap View and reports the first current output. No timer, synthetic callback or weakened test is introduced. A stale/detached/old lease returns before this transition.
- This closes the API-35 RED at the actual producer-to-controller boundary. It is still not a Nothing pacing result; the revised source must pass the native job, Human APK lane, exact-source graph regeneration and device validation before handoff.

### Follow-up: Main hand-off slot retirement safety

- The same retained API-35 artifact logged `HardwareBuffer.close` without a matching application close and a release callback posting to a dead renderer Handler after teardown. This is a producer resource-lifetime violation, not harmless diagnostic noise.
- Cause: a completed frame was represented only as `READY` until Main later marked it compositor-owned. If retirement/disposal won that short interval, it could close the buffer and quit the worker even though Main had a posted ready-frame hand-off or SurfaceControl could still issue a release callback.
- Candidate correction: `READY_FOR_MAIN` now represents the bounded hand-off owner. Retire/dispose retain `RENDERING`, `READY_FOR_MAIN` and `COMPOSITOR_OWNED` slots. The Main hand-off either changes the exact slot to compositor-owned or drops/finishes the retired slot; only then may worker shutdown occur. This preserves one in-flight render, the fixed three-slot bound and Main non-blocking behavior.

### Source-proven defects and reachable failure paths at 81c8d4b

1. Incorrect lower-level screenshot target:
   - The compositor test creates a separate TYPE_APPLICATION_PANEL through TestPanelWindowManager, but copyWindow calls PixelCopy.request(activity.window, ...).
   - PixelCopy of the Activity window targets that window's Surface, not a whole-display composite including a separately added panel. This assertion is not a valid oracle for the child attached to the panel.
   - The real-service fixture uses a compositor screenshot and therefore independently demonstrates a real visible-output failure. Fixing the false target must not be used to dismiss that failure.

2. Fixed-pool recovery can shrink to a self-stalling single slot:
   - KeyguardOrbBufferRenderer.Worker.retire changes owned slots to RETIRED but keeps FREE slots.
   - release, dropReady and stale render completion remove retired slots.
   - ensureResources returns true for a matching-size pool containing ANY non-retired slot; it never replenishes a partially depleted pool in that branch.
   - Reachable schedule: A compositor-owned, B rendering, C free -> retirement -> A/B safely finish and are removed -> only C remains -> C is published and becomes compositor-owned -> no free target exists for the replacement transaction that would release C. The existing guard keeps returning true without restoring capacity.
   - This is a source-demonstrable liveness defect. A deterministic production-state-machine test must reproduce it; the exact slot schedule causing the retained CI failures has not been proven.

3. Retirement destroys the ownership information required by disposal:
   - Controller disposal calls stop/onDetached/retire and renderer.dispose; renderer.dispose retires again.
   - Worker.retire collapses RENDERING, READY_FOR_MAIN and COMPOSITOR_OWNED into RETIRED.
   - Worker.dispose's awaitingRelease filter includes only the three pre-retirement states and excludes RETIRED. It can consequently close buffers still owned by GPU/handoff/compositor and end the callback owner early.
   - Retirement must be orthogonal to owner/fence state; repeated retire/dispose must be idempotent. An enum rename or another special-case filter is not a complete state-machine repair.

4. Fence and resize safety are incomplete:
   - Stale/error render completion and dropReady close the render-result fence and can free/remove a buffer without establishing that GPU use has finished.
   - ensureResources' resize protection covers COMPOSITOR_OWNED/RETIRED but does not independently protect RENDERING/READY_FOR_MAIN before closing the pool.
   - release waits indefinitely for a release fence on the sole worker Handler, blocking its own configure/retire/recovery processing.
   - A transaction-committed callback is not a buffer-release callback. The Android API requires waiting on a valid release fence before reuse. Never treat a timeout or discarded callback as permission to reuse or close an owned buffer.

5. The isolation and LIVE boundary remain incomplete:
   - Every onFrameReady posts to Main, and publishReady performs setBuffer and setVisibility(true) there. Steady-state publication remains dependent on the service Main queue.
   - The first-publication callback changes controller state/hides bootstrap BEFORE applyTransactionOnDraw/direct apply returns; queued-on-draw is not physical presentation. Controller onAttached also uses LIVE before current output exists.
   - Separate desired eligibility, current-lease GPU readiness, transaction queue/submission/commit and physical visibility evidence. Do not fabricate a legacy CPU shader draw or physical timestamp from a backend-control callback.
   - Passing a valid presentation fence to SurfaceControl is a supported Android operation; it is NOT by itself an API misuse. The unresolved design issue is coupling visibility/control to unready rendering and failing to preserve lifetime on dropped/retired frames.

### Reviewer numerical reproducer (not GPU runtime validation)

The following scratch-only Python/NumPy evaluation was executed by the reviewer. SHA256 of the original script: `6c15a8bc3974ec8689b15ce0f326621cd54a21bfe08bf1e57f07f6037c2da4a4`. It must not replace Android correctness tests or be copied into production rendering.

```python
import numpy as np

# Reviewer-only numeric evaluation of the unchanged dualTide equations.
# This is not Android/GPU runtime evidence and is not production shader code.
F=np.float32
def fract(v): return v-np.floor(v)
def hash_(v,seed):
    c=np.floor(v)
    a=fract(c[...,[0,1,0]]*F(.1031)+F(seed)*F(.0173))
    d=np.sum(a*(a[...,[1,2,0]]+F(33.33)),axis=-1)
    a=a+d[...,None]
    return fract((a[...,0]+a[...,1])*a[...,2])
def noise(v,seed):
    c=np.floor(v); fr=fract(v); e=fr*fr*(F(3)-F(2)*fr)
    a=hash_(c,seed); b=hash_(c+np.array([1,0],dtype=F),seed)
    top=a+(b-a)*e[...,0]
    a=hash_(c+np.array([0,1],dtype=F),seed); b=hash_(c+F(1),seed)
    bot=a+(b-a)*e[...,0]
    return top+(bot-top)*e[...,1]
def fbm(v,seed):
    total=np.zeros(v.shape[:-1],dtype=F); amp=F(.58); norm=F(0); freq=F(1)
    for i in range(3):
        total += noise(v*freq,F(seed)+F(i)*F(17.3))*amp
        norm+=amp; freq*=F(1.93); amp*=F(.46)
    return total/norm
def evaluate(phase,settings=None):
    m=np.full(40,.2,dtype=F) if settings is None else np.array(settings,dtype=F)
    y,x=np.mgrid[0:168,0:168].astype(F)
    uv=np.stack([(x+F(.5))/F(168),(y+F(.5))/F(168)],axis=-1)
    p=F(.5)+(uv-F(.5))*max(F(.01),m[5]); phase=F(phase); pi=F(np.pi)
    ratio=m[2]+np.sin(phase*m[4]*pi*F(2))*m[3]; mt=phase*m[7]
    broad=(fbm(p*np.array([1.17,1.09],dtype=F)+np.array([mt*F(.07),-mt*F(.05)],dtype=F),31.7)-F(.5))*m[6]
    fine=(fbm(p*np.array([2.8,2.5],dtype=F)+np.array([-mt*F(.09),mt*F(.08)],dtype=F),67.3)-F(.5))*m[9]
    field=p[...,0]+ratio+broad*F(.20)+fine*F(.12)
    ap=phase*F(.52); bp=phase*F(.47)+m[23]*pi/F(180)
    ax=F(.5)-m[18]*F(.5)+np.sin(ap*F(.83))*m[15]+(F(.5)+F(.5)*np.sin(ap*F(.31)))*m[17]
    bx=F(.5)+m[18]*F(.5)-np.sin(bp*F(.79))*m[15]-(F(.5)+F(.5)*np.sin(bp*F(.29)))*m[17]
    ay=F(.5)+np.sin(ap*F(.61))*m[16]; by=F(.5)-np.sin(bp*F(.57))*m[16]
    def mass(cx,cy,rx,ry):
        d=(p-np.array([cx,cy],dtype=F))/np.maximum(np.array([rx,ry],dtype=F),F(.0001))
        return np.exp(-np.sum(d*d,axis=-1))
    am=mass(ax,ay,m[19],m[19]/max(F(.01),m[21])); bm=mass(bx,by,m[20],m[20]/max(F(.01),m[22]))
    warp=(fbm(p*m[26]+np.array([phase*m[27]*F(.11),-phase*m[27]*F(.09)],dtype=F),103.2)-F(.5))*m[25]
    field+=warp+(bm-am)*m[24]*F(.46)
    local=(am+bm-F(.7))*m[12]*F(.12)
    soft=max(F(.001),m[8]); t=np.clip((field-(F(.5)-soft))/max(F(.000001),F(2)*soft),0,1)
    mixture=t*t*(F(3)-F(2)*t); seam=F(4)*mixture*(F(1)-mixture)
    pulse=np.sin(phase*m[11]*pi*F(2))*m[10]
    light=np.clip((pulse+(broad+fine)*m[12]+local)*seam,-.25,.25)
    size=np.array([390,220],dtype=F); direction=np.array([.9271838546,.3746065934],dtype=F)
    length=np.sum(abs(direction)*size); start=size*F(.5)-direction*length*F(.5)
    base=np.clip(np.sum((uv*size-start)*direction,axis=-1)/length,0,1)
    coordinate=np.clip(base+(mixture-p[...,0])*np.clip(m[0],0,1)*F(4)*base*(F(1)-base),0,1)
    cols=np.array([[16,79,124],[98,199,220],[131,102,220]],dtype=F)/F(255)
    amt=np.where(coordinate<=F(.5),coordinate*F(2),(coordinate-F(.5))*F(2))
    rgb=np.where((coordinate<=F(.5))[...,None],cols[0]+(cols[1]-cols[0])*amt[...,None],cols[1]+(cols[2]-cols[1])*amt[...,None])
    rgb=np.clip(rgb*(F(1)+light[...,None]),0,1)
    mask=(x-F(83.5))**2+(y-F(83.5))**2<F(80)**2
    stats=dict(phase=float(phase),ratio=float(ratio),field_min=float(field[mask].min()),field_max=float(field[mask].max()),mixture_min=float(mixture[mask].min()),mixture_max=float(mixture[mask].max()),max_abs_light=float(abs(light[mask]).max()))
    return np.rint(rgb*F(255)).astype(int),mask,stats

if __name__=='__main__':
    phases=[1.196795,1.5234617,.97574466,1.8890779,.25,.35,3.75]
    images=[]
    for ph in phases:
        im,mask,stats=evaluate(ph);images.append(im);print(stats)
    for a,b in [(0,1),(2,3),(4,5),(4,6),(0,6)]:
        delta=abs(images[a]-images[b]).max(axis=-1)[mask]
        print('PAIR',phases[a],phases[b],dict(changed_ge7=int((delta>=7).sum()),sum_delta=int(delta.sum()),max_delta=int(delta.max())))
```

### New concrete diagnosis: numeric equality is incorrectly used as CAS identity

File at the reviewed SHA: `android/app/src/androidTest/kotlin/com/fluvi/app/lockscreen/KeyguardServiceOverlayInstrumentationTest.kt`, ProducerPixelProbe lines 379–431.

```kotlin
private val requestedPhase = AtomicReference<Float?>(null)
// awaitPhase:
requestedPhase.set(phase)
// onProduced:
val phase = requestedPhase.get() ?: return
// ... matching phase, fence wait, successful pixel copy ...
if (requestedPhase.compareAndSet(phase, null)) captured.set(sample)
```

- AtomicReference.compareAndSet compares object reference identity, not floating-point numeric equality. The non-null local Float is unboxed and boxed again at the CAS boundary; its expected reference is not the object stored by set(phase). Thus a correct phase and successful readback can be discarded, captured remains null, and awaitPhase emits a misleading 'producer did not reach requested phase' timeout.
- This is a source-level sufficient failure mechanism, reproduced independently. The current CI does not log every readback/CAS outcome, so the reviewer does not claim all intermediate Android callbacks have been traced.
- Strong corroboration from the actual CI compile log at 2026-11-11T19:28:38.6891933Z: `KeyguardServiceOverlayInstrumentationTest.kt:414:25 This call may have inconsistent results because 'AtomicReference' uses identity equality and 'Float?' does not have a consistent identity.`
- Reviewer ran the minimal equivalent Kotlin/JVM sequence below, first with Kotlin 2.2.0 and then **the project's exact Kotlin 2.2.20** (as declared in android/settings.gradle.kts), JRE 21.0.13. Both returned: `Float phase CAS success=0/100; request-token CAS success=100/100`. Kotlin 2.2.20 also emitted the same identity warning. This is an executed JVM reproducer, not Android instrumentation or a phone performance result.
- Official reference: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/24/docs/api/java.base/java/util/concurrent/atomic/AtomicReference.html#compareAndSet(V,V)

```kotlin
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference

fun main() {
    val requestedPhase = AtomicReference<Float?>(null)
    var legacySuccess = 0
    repeat(100) {
        requestedPhase.set(1.196795f)
        val phase = requestedPhase.get() ?: error("missing")
        check(kotlin.math.abs(1.196795f - phase) <= .0001f)
        if (requestedPhase.compareAndSet(phase, null)) legacySuccess++
    }
    data class Request(val id: Long, val phase: Float)
    val requested = AtomicReference<Request?>(null)
    var tokenSuccess = 0
    repeat(100) {
        requested.set(Request(it.toLong(), 1.196795f))
        val request = requested.get() ?: error("missing")
        if (requested.compareAndSet(request, null)) tokenSuccess++
    }
    println("Float phase CAS success=$legacySuccess/100; request-token CAS success=$tokenSuccess/100")
    check(legacySuccess == 0)
    check(tokenSuccess == 100)
}
```

### Bounded correction required before another backend hypothesis

1. Replace AtomicReference<Float?> with an immutable **request identity object**, carrying monotonically increasing request id, expected phase, expected current lease and per-request completion/result. Retain the exact request object read by onProduced for CAS. Phase tolerance is for numerical frame matching only. Do not replace this with getAndSet(null), a boxed Double, a blind set(null) or a larger timeout: those either retain the identity bug or let a late A clear B.
2. Results/errors must belong to that request, not a single shared captured/failure slot. Test success with correct phase, mismatched phase, old lease, superseded request, duplicate delivery and A1 -> B -> A2 at the same numeric A phase. A late A1 callback must neither satisfy A2 nor cancel B. Arm a request before advancing controlled time; use current lease/frame/use identity as well as phase. The regression must exercise the actual probe acknowledgement path (or its extracted shared implementation), not merely a lambda returning a constant.
3. Rerun this focused acknowledgement regression first, then the calibrated service gate. Keep A/C expected equality, A/B meaningful difference and A-return checks. Gather both producer and compositor evidence before assertions terminate a scenario. Producer readback occurs before publication; completion of awaitPhase alone is not proof that the compositor crop has switched to B. Wait for exact current-lease publication/observed crop under a bounded condition, recording identities; a transaction callback is not physical presentation.
4. Repair both remaining lower motion oracles with the same profile/program/size and calibrated phases. Keep meaningful-motion thresholds and negative controls. The current A/C assertion merely rejects 'meaningful motion'; also define a tight explicit equality/error bound so widespread small divergence does not pass as parity.
5. Keep deterministic phase calibration separate from actual animation/performance. Current fixture holds C during its ten-second steady interval, so counters during that interval cannot establish advancing material time. Return to the production monotonic clock for genuine animation/performance and disable readback; retain OFF/LIGHT/FULL separation.
6. Preserve the exact-grant and nullable-receipt source repairs. Still require real worker retire-A / install-B / unblock-A integration and null-fence receipt ordering evidence; the new container unit tests do not complete that contract.
7. Resolve the independent diagnostic export assertion and dashboard readiness failure with their own evidence. Do not weaken unrelated gates or emit a Human APK while required gates are red.
8. The prior full implementation contract remains in force: matched backend evidence, slot reuse, bounded recovery, lifecycle cases, physical validation user-only. A new RuntimeShader per frame, renderer replacement or shader simplification is not justified by this first-A timeout. Do not spend another broad build cycle interpreting a broken test acknowledgement as frozen GPU output.

### Source findings and falsifiable hypotheses

H1 — acquisition plus Main result-delivery delay (measured boundary; exact Main blocker unresolved).
- Service processInspectionQueue acquires off Main, then awaits withContext(Dispatchers.Main.immediate) before completing its one-wide inspection queue. A pending acquisition can therefore be held behind application delivery. KeyguardSystemStateSampler likewise clears active and starts pending only inside its Main callback. These are source-proven coupling points, not proof that changing their queue ownership alone eliminates the measured89ms.
- Recurring system acquisition ALREADY has its own executor. ACTION_USER_PRESENT ALREADY directly calls hideImmediately. Do not prescribe either old fix again.
- ADMISSION and PUBLICATION fresh system reads can still execute on Main by design; their actual contribution to request261 is unknown. Other candidates include ViewRoot/RenderThread wait, GC/descheduling, owned callback work and framework work. Handler.createAsync does not preempt a busy Main thread; a blanket async/front-of-queue change is not a diagnosis.
- KeyguardMainWorkEvidence retains32 owned scopes and selects up to3 overlaps, but current snapshots are attached to retained material DRAW_GAP samples. The isolated captures contain no such samples. Reuse bounded numeric evidence for slow inspection handoff/pre-enqueue/first-output intervals, with wall/CPU timestamps and incomplete-coverage flags; do not build another unbounded recorder.
- Required experiment: distinguish callback->system enqueue->worker start->public getter start/end->Main post/entry->inspection enqueue, and inspection finish->Main entry. Use matching trace thread-state/Binder/RenderThread evidence if owned spans do not cover the gap. Then repair the demonstrated blocking work or result-delivery coupling, preserving exact authority, one active acquisition and bounded latest pending/result storage. A worker cannot perform View/WindowManager operations.

H2 — actual isolated renderer is not prepared by service-start GPU preparation (source-proven preparation gap; causal contribution to197ms/2-frame anomaly must be tested).
- KeyguardCardWindow.prepareRetainedView invokes materialController.prepare, which only invokes prepareSelectedPrograms. At initial service preparation, isolatedOrbRequested is false and latestOrbScene is null; reconcileIsolatedOrbTarget cannot initialize/configure the lazy isolated backend.
- AndroidKeyguardGpuMaterialPreparer creates a separate HardwareRenderer/ImageReader and its own shader, draws once, then destroys those objects. Its READY record is not readiness of KeyguardOrbBufferRenderer's persistent pool/renderers/slot shaders.
- The first authorized show calls updateMaterialForPresentation; only then does controller.update set isolatedOrbRequested/latestOrbScene, initialize the lazy isolated renderer and configure its resources. Worker.ensureResources allocates up to3 HardwareBuffers/HardwareBufferRenderers; prepareSlotShaders initializes slot-local shaders later. The existing "detached prewarm" starts immediately before addView and is not service-start preparation of this exact pipeline.
- New justified repair candidate: an explicit bounded detached preparation phase for the selected isolated ORB backend, separated from presentation authority. Prepare/reuse the SAME bounded resource owner for the exact material/size; never relabel an old attachment's rendered frame as current. A fresh current lease must still authorize fresh output. No continuous hidden animation, extra per-attachment pools, Main wait or new show permission.

Then implement this narrow preparation refactor and demonstrate baseline/candidate setup removal and real current output. Do not claim all show or hide latency solved by prewarming.

- Worker.render silently returns when ANY slot is READY_FOR_MAIN or RENDERING. Its no-FREE branch alone increments dropped. A slow producer callback, queued first Main bind/worker acknowledgement, running/callback liveness issue, or retired slot still draining can stop progress without a large dropped count.

Official contracts rechecked:
- https://developer.android.com/reference/android/graphics/HardwareBufferRenderer — HardwareBufferRenderer and HardwareRenderer share the render thread; a separate HandlerThread does not imply a separate GPU/RenderThread.
- https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/AttachedSurfaceControl — applyTransactionOnDraw associates with the next hierarchy draw; queueing does not prove physical presentation. Current code explicitly invalidates, so "missing invalidate" is not an established bug.
